members.title: Prime Minister arrives in Tokyo on 4-day official visit
members.lead: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman arrived in Tokyo Monday morning (local time) on a four-day official visit at the invitation of his Japanese counterpart Sanae Takaichi, aiming to deepen bilateral ties, attract investment and expand trade and development cooperation. A Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight carrying the prime minister, his wife Zubaida Rahman, and members of his entourage landed at Narita International Airport at 9:07 am local time. The prime minister was received at the airport by State Minister for Foreign Affairs Yasutaka Nakasone. A motorcade then escorted him to Tokyo’s Imperial Hotel, where he will stay during his visit. .Japan to invest Tk 774.7 billion in Bangladesh. Prime Minister’s Adviser for Posts, Telecommunications and Information Technology and Science and Technology Rehan Asif Asad, Special Assistant to the Prime Minister for Foreign Employment in the Asia-Pacific region Md Shakirul Islam Khan, and senior officials of the Bangladesh Embassy in Tokyo were also present. Earlier, the prime minister left Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka early today Bangladesh time for Japan aboard a Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight, accompanied by a small delegation. Tarique Rahman is scheduled to hold a high-level bilateral talk with Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi at her office on 27 October, followed by a joint press announcement and a luncheon hosted by the Japanese premier, according to the Prime Minister’s press wing. . During the four-day visit, the prime minister will also meet Japanese government officials, development institutions and business leaders, visit industrial and energy facilities, and deliver the keynote address at the Bangladesh-Japan Economic Forum. members.title: PM discusses skills partnership, innovation city with JICA chief
members.lead: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman today discussed proposals for a Bangladesh-Japan Skills Partnership and a Technological Village and Innovation City, alongside cooperation in agricultural modernisation, agro-processing and light engineering, with Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) President Dr Akihiko Tanaka. The proposals came up during a courtesy meeting between Prime Minister and JICA President at Hotel Imperial here at 5:10 pm local time, said Deputy Press Secretary to the Prime Minister Shahadat Shadhin. During the meeting, the Bangladesh side placed the proposals for the Bangladesh-Japan Skills Partnership and the establishment of a Technological Village and Innovation City, as well as expanding cooperation in agricultural modernisation, agro-processing and the light engineering sector. . At the beginning of the meeting, Tarique Rahman recalled his fruitful meeting with the JICA president in Dhaka during the latter’s visit to Bangladesh in July this year. The Prime Minister expressed gratitude for Japan’s long standing cooperation and JICA’s significant contributions to Bangladesh’s socioeconomic development. Highlighting Japan’s important role in Bangladesh’s infrastructure development, socioeconomic progress and efforts to realise its development aspirations, the premier said, “It is essential to continue cooperation with Japan to further deepen the longstanding friendly relations between the two countries, advance Bangladesh’s development and improve people’s living standards.” . The meeting also emphasised the need to complete major ongoing development projects supported by Japan within their stipulated deadlines. The two sides also discussed expediting the approval and implementation of priority projects awaiting approval. Tarique Rahman emphasised the need to continue concessional loan assistance and expand technical cooperation in line with Bangladesh’s current development priorities. members.title: PM seeks Japan’s support to modernise KAFCO, explore 2nd fertiliser plant
members.lead: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman today sought Japan’s cooperation in modernising the Karnaphuli Fertilizer Company Limited (KAFCO) and exploring the possibility of establishing a second fertiliser factory in Bangladesh as part of his government’s efforts to strengthen bilateral economic ties and attract Japanese investment. He made the call during a courtesy meeting with Masumi Kakinoki, chairman of Marubeni Corporation and president of the Japan-Bangladesh Committee for Commercial and Economic Cooperation (JBCCEC), at Hotel Imperial in Tokyo this afternoon (local time), said PM’s Deputy Press Secretary Shahadat Shadhin. During the meeting, the Prime Minister called for increased Japanese investment in Bangladesh’s promising sectors, including information and communication technology (ICT), renewable energy and advanced manufacturing, highlighting significant opportunities through foreign direct investment (FDI) and public-private partnerships (PPPs). . Tarique Rahman said, “The government is committed to creating an investment-friendly environment by reforming regulations, simplifying investment approval procedures and strengthening public-private partnerships to make it easier for Japanese businesses to invest and operate in Bangladesh.” He also praised Kakinoki’s leadership in promoting trade and economic cooperation between Bangladesh and Japan and thanked him for his role in expanding Japanese investment in Bangladesh and strengthening bilateral business ties. Kakinoki expressed the hope that the effective implementation of the Economic Partnership Agreement (EPA) between the two countries would expand bilateral trade, increase Japanese investment and create new business opportunities. .
